title: Restriction, extension and coextension of scalars
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a monoidal category and let $\varphi\colon\mathcal R\to\mathcal S$ be a
morphism of monoid objects ([sk-def-sfb-ring-object]). Module objects are as in
[sk-def-sfb-module-objects].

1. **Restriction.** The functor
   $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\colon\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$
   gives $N$ the action
   $\mathcal R\otimes N\xrightarrow{\varphi\otimes N}\mathcal S\otimes N\xrightarrow{\gamma_N}N$.
   It is the identity on underlying objects and morphisms, so it commutes with the forgetful
   functors.
2. **Extension.** Let $\mathcal C$ be braided with coequalizers, with $X\otimes-$ and
   $-\otimes X$ preserving colimits for every $X$, and let $\mathcal R$ be commutative. Define
   $$
   \operatorname{Ext}_\varphi(M)=\mathcal S\otimes_{\mathcal R}M:=\operatorname{coeq}\Bigl(
   \mathcal S\otimes\mathcal R\otimes M\rightrightarrows\mathcal S\otimes M\Bigr),
   $$
   the coequalizer of $\bigl(\mu_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal S\otimes\varphi)\bigr)\otimes M$ and
   $(\mathcal S\otimes\gamma_M)\alpha$, with $\mathcal S$ acting on the first factor. This
   is a functor $\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)$, left
   adjoint to $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$. Hence $\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi$ preserves every finite colimit that exists
   in its source (so is right exact whenever its source has finite colimits), and
   $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ preserves limits.
3. **Coextension.** Let $\mathcal C$ be closed with equalizers, and write
   $\underline{\Hom}(X,-)$ for the right adjoint of $X\otimes-$. Define
   $$
   \operatorname{Coext}_\varphi(N)=\Hom_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal S,N):=\operatorname{eq}\Bigl(
   \underline{\Hom}(\mathcal S,N)\rightrightarrows\underline{\Hom}(\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal S,N)\Bigr).
   $$
   The first map precomposes with the action $\mu_{\mathcal S}(\varphi\otimes\mathcal S)$ of
   $\mathcal R$ on $\mathcal S$, and the second postcomposes with the action of $\mathcal R$
   on $N$. Here $\mathcal S$ acts by right multiplication on the source, $(s\cdot f)(t)=f(ts)$.
   This is a functor $\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)$, right
   adjoint to $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$. Hence $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ preserves
   colimits.
4. Under the hypotheses of 2 and 3,
   $\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi\dashv\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\dashv\operatorname{Coext}_\varphi$.
   If $\mathcal C$ is moreover abelian with $\otimes$ additive in each variable, then both
   module categories are abelian ([lem-sfb-modobj-abelian]) and
   $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ is exact.
5. **Invertible $\varphi$.** Under the hypotheses of 2 and 3, let $\varphi$ be an
   isomorphism. Then $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ is an equivalence with quasi-inverse
   $\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi^{-1}}$, and
   $$
   \operatorname{Ext}_\varphi\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi^{-1}}\cong\operatorname{Coext}_\varphi .
   $$

proof.text: For clause 1, apply [def-sfb-modobj-restriction] to the given monoid morphism $\varphi$. Its statement gives the $\mathcal R$-action $\gamma_N\circ(\varphi\otimes N)$, its module axioms, and functoriality on $\mathcal S$-linear morphisms. Because its underlying objects and arrows are unchanged, composing with the forgetful functor gives precisely the original forgetful functor on $\mathcal S$-modules.

Under the hypotheses of clause 2, [def-sfb-modobj-extension] applies: the category is braided, has coequalizers, tensoring on either side preserves colimits, and $\mathcal R$ is commutative. It constructs the displayed coequalizer $\mathcal S\otimes_{\mathcal R}M$, with left $\mathcal S$-action induced from multiplication on the first factor, and sends $f$ to the map induced by $\mathcal S\otimes f$. Thus the object and arrow assignments in clause 2 form the asserted functor.

The natural Hom-set bijection of [def-sfb-modobj-extend-restrict-adjunction] gives $\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi\dashv\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ for the functors just constructed. Explicitly, it sends $g$ to $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(g)\circ u_M$, where $u_M$ is insertion of the unit followed by the coequalizer projection. Under exactly these extension hypotheses, [lem-sfb-modobj-extension-right-exact] gives preservation of finite colimits and [lem-sfb-modobj-restriction-preserves-limits] gives preservation of limits by restriction. The right-exact terminology is used with the finite-colimit existence condition of [def-galois-exact-functor]; no existence of an initial object follows merely from coequalizers.

Under the independent hypotheses of clause 3 (closed monoidal, with equalizers), [def-sfb-modobj-coextension] constructs the equalizer $E=\Hom_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal S,N)$. Its first arrow is precomposition with the left $\mathcal R$-action on $\mathcal S$; its second arrow is the adjoint of $\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal S\otimes\underline{\Hom}(\mathcal S,N)\xrightarrow{\mathcal R\otimes\mathrm{ev}}\mathcal R\otimes N\xrightarrow{\gamma_N}N$. The same cited statement gives the left $\mathcal S$-action, adjoint to multiplication followed by evaluation, and postcomposition on morphisms. In the formula $(s\cdot f)(t)=f(ts)$, $t$ is the first and $s$ the second multiplicative input: this is right multiplication on the source. No braiding or commutativity is required here.

The natural Hom-set bijection in [def-sfb-modobj-restrict-coextend-adjunction] gives $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\dashv\operatorname{Coext}_\varphi$. It is evaluation at the unit, with inverse $f\mapsto(m\mapsto(s\mapsto f(sm)))$, so the right adjoint is the equalizer functor of the preceding step. Under these same hypotheses [lem-sfb-modobj-restriction-preserves-colimits] states that restriction preserves colimits. This proves the rest of clause 3.

For clause 4, impose both sets of hypotheses. The two preceding adjunctions then involve the same restriction functor, giving the asserted chain. If $\mathcal C$ is abelian and tensoring is additive in each variable, the assumed colimit preservation of $\mathcal R\otimes-$ and $\mathcal S\otimes-$ includes finite colimits. Apply [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] first to $\mathcal R$ and then to $\mathcal S$. Its conclusion is that both module categories are abelian. It requires neither commutativity of $\mathcal S$ nor exactness of tensoring.

source.place: paragraph 4, adjunction chain and abelian module categories

proof.text: In the abelian case of clause 4, restriction preserves limits by [lem-sfb-modobj-restriction-preserves-limits] and colimits by [lem-sfb-modobj-restriction-preserves-colimits]. Finite limits and colimits exist directly from [def-sp-abelian]: for a finite diagram $D$, its limit is the kernel of $d:\bigoplus_iD(i)\to\bigoplus_{a:i\to j}D(j)$ with $a$-component $D(a)\pi_i-\pi_j$, and its colimit is the cokernel of $e:\bigoplus_{a:i\to j}D(i)\to\bigoplus_iD(i)$ whose restriction to the $a$-summand is $\iota_jD(a)-\iota_i$. The equation $dh=0$ is precisely the cone condition, and $ke=0$ is precisely the cocone condition; the kernel and cokernel universal properties therefore give the required universal cones and cocones. Empty sums are the zero object, so empty diagrams are included. Restriction thus preserves all finite limits and finite colimits that exist in these categories. By [def-galois-exact-functor] (Stacks tag 0034, definition-exact), these properties give left and right exactness, hence exactness.

Under clause 5, [def-sfb-modobj-restriction-equivalence] gives the equivalence $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ with quasi-inverse $\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi^{-1}}$. Its hypotheses are exactly the simultaneous extension and coextension hypotheses together with invertibility of the monoid morphism; in particular it does not require an abelian category.

Finally [def-sfb-modobj-extension-along-iso] gives $a:\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi^{-1}}$, and [def-sfb-modobj-coextension-along-iso] gives $b:\operatorname{Coext}_\varphi\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi^{-1}}$, under the hypotheses verified in the preceding step. Invert $b$ to obtain the second arrow in the asserted chain. If one also wants the direct comparison, it is $b^{-1}\circ a$; its inverse is $a^{-1}\circ b$, with the inverse identities following by cancellation. No separate node for composition of these isomorphisms is needed.
